Ernst Julius Günther Röhm ( German: [ɛʁnst ˈʁøːm] ; 28 November 1887 – 1 July 1934) was a German military officer, politician,  and a leading member of the Nazi Party . A close friend and early ally of Adolf Hitler , Röhm was the co-founder and leader of the Sturmabteilung (SA), the Nazi Party's original paramilitary wing, which played a significant role in Hitler's rise to power . He served as chief of the SA from 1931 until his assassination by the SS in 1934 during the Night of the Long Knives .
